milestone: Hosted editor gamepad input with shared device configuration and human controls
implemented: Hosted SDL mode updates devices without owner-thread Windows message pumping; both desktop.input.devices and the generic input.devices route use that host.

Stable evaluator ownership and staged device acquisition preserve prior assignment, focus and pending input on invalid reconfiguration. Stop/session replacement disconnects before evaluator destruction; SDL reference ownership survives for later discovery.

One assigned controller, disabled/only-connected/explicit policies, explicit v2 defaults or frozen profiles; v1 plus enabled gamepad is rejected without conversion. Start releases existing Game input only.

Per-tick native evaluation preserves analog rate across catch-up and consumes keyboard/mouse/gamepad edges once after commit. Focus, capture suspension, remapping and lifecycle transitions reapply neutral gating.
Bounded gamepad event removal and mapped raw-joystick duplicate cleanup preserve unrelated SDL events and retain removed-device overflow identities until drained.

Game Input window provides profile/default choice, device discovery/selection and assignment/arming/error status. Stopped preferences are staged for the next capture; active Apply uses shared native validation before releasing managed capture.

native_bridge.note: Same bridge source compiled directly with SDL for process-local virtual devices; no test RPCs in the production DLL. Positive control proves a real SDL pump dispatches the sentinel.

final_bridge_regressions.name: keyboard
checks: Frozen controller discovery and strict playing/Game-camera focus gates work without requiring graphics.
Real controller movement/jump/yaw matches evaluated controls; held movement persists, while look/jump/use consume once and repeat events/receipts cannot retrigger them.
Invalid batches validate atomically; reserved/gamepad/type/shape/count errors preserve pending input and failed receipts are reusable.
Eight-tick catch-up drains independent mouse frames -180/-180/-70 then zero, preserves held movement, and consumes jump/use once; exact frames feed independent replay.
Focus loss, Pause and Scene switch clear held controls and pending edges; explicit reacquisition does not restore stale movement.
Persisted rebound profile changes actual movement and yaw/pitch; stale profile revisions reject without disturbing the old evaluator.
Stop/new session drops configuration and rejects stale events; independent semantic replay exactly matches final controller/camera state with unchanged authored bytes/history.
After actual recursive authored deletion, frozen runtime controller/camera discovery, configuration and movement remain valid; Stop restores the now-empty authored controller list.

final_bridge_regressions.name: playback
checks: Playback/view schemas are discoverable; invalid camera selection is atomic and Game excludes Scene interaction tools.
Paused clock and detached draw remain inert; Step advances exactly once with core receipt retry and strict session guards.
Only owner poll advances real time; long stalls cap at eight ticks, competing runtime mutations reject, and paused wall time never catches up.
Existing runtime.start/stop synchronize with the desktop driver, defaulting external starts to paused.
Game uses the same runtime with its frozen camera lens and hierarchy despite authored camera edits and deletion.
A genuine animation sampling failure preserves automatic ticks15–17 and pauses before18; explicit four-tick Step still rolls back all state, with unchanged authored bytes/history.

summary.platform: Windows x86_64 via WSL native interop

checks: Generated schemas match native fingerprints; sorted paged query, all typed reads, optional absence, liveness and staged writes run through actual C# Tick
Duplicate, explicit exception, later-tick exception, NaN, dangling reference and unknown entity all roll back component bytes/revision/global state/tick; later valid write recovers
Compatible CLR reorder/labels preserve native values, changed defaults reject without swap, 100 real CoreCLR reloads collect all retired modules
Exact component membership/state/revision and C# values restore transactionally; stale component-only save/load guards reject and old receipts never replay mutation
Fresh process restores native-owned custom components with trusted CoreCLR/NativeAOT configuration and continues generated C# writes
Actual generated C# Tick saves/restores native components through owner coordination; same-owner ticket stays terminal, fresh-owner old ticket expires, and source-step retry cannot replay the load

limitations: Headless managed ABI and actual CoreCLR/native-engine regression; no new GUI or physical input claim.
NativeAOT artifacts were not republished for this unchanged gameplay SDK interface milestone.

initial_failures.detail: Native fixture JSON initializer missed a closing brace. Fixed the fixture; production source unchanged.
Harness assumed two attached viewports in default tabbed layout; all 54 input actions passed. Corrected fixture explicitly uses split views; production unchanged.

warnings: Existing GCC variable-tracking fallback in world schema description.
Two existing obsolete Avalonia bitmap-save overload warnings.
review.visual: Attached Game Input client render inspected: readable labels/status and no clipped controls. Windows locked (flags 0); this is not an OS screenshot.

limitations: Virtual devices and synthetic/semantic controls do not qualify physical Xbox/DualSense controllers, Bluetooth, real focus/cursor confinement, input latency, IME or accessibility.
Standalone SDL fixture enables test-owned background input; production makes no global background hint change. Direct bridge fixture uses SDL video, no background hint and hidden owned HWNDs.
Capture suspension is qualified through a real queued capture timing out without drawing. This is not a rendered gamepad capture or subjective gameplay-feel test.
One assigned local controller. General action maps, haptics/gyro, controller-only editor navigation, multiplayer routing and console APIs remain unfinished. Editor audio output remains unconnected.

At most 256 gamepad and 256 mapped raw duplicate events are removed per poll. SDL_FilterEvents traverses the existing queue; no constant-time, no-allocation or sustained frame-budget claim. Profiler scope input.gamepad.poll attributes this work.
GUI choices are session-local. Live device IDs are process-session identities, not persisted hardware identities. No profile conversion or automatic focus acquisition.

Both tested Windows GPUs belong to one laptop. No Linux hardware rendering, physical-controller or console qualification is established by these runs. NVRHI error counts are not full Vulkan validation.
